title: San Francisco Rent Increase Review
subtitle: Outer Sunset · ZIP 94122 · reported two-unit property
privacy_notice: Public records use neutral unit and resident aliases. Dates and amounts below are user-reported, not authenticated. Identifying initials, addresses, and APNs are not published.
disclaimer: Independent research and conditional arithmetic—not legal advice, a Rent Board determination, an appraisal, or attorney approval. Unknown values remain blank and flagged.

pages.title: Know the limit. Verify the facts. Defend the reason.
pages.description: A source-linked review of local, state, and federal rules for a reported 1940-built two-unit property. The ordinary local rate is clear; permission to raise either unit is not yet established.

sections.title: No increase is authorized by this dashboard
sections.text: Coverage, current lawful base rent, anniversary, prior increases, banking, inventory/license status, and notice have not been verified. A reported building age or lease amount cannot substitute for those records.

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.description: Each conclusion is separated from the facts still needed for this property.

rows.question: What is the ordinary local increase?
rows.answer: 1.6% of verified base rent for the stated effective-date interval, subject to all conditions.
rows.boundary: Neither unit's lawful base rent or coverage is verified.

rows.question: Is a market catch-up increase normal or lawful?
rows.answer: A long-standing below-market tenancy alone is not an extraordinary circumstance supporting a special-circumstances petition.
rows.boundary: No extraordinary circumstances or comparable-unit evidence were supplied.

rows.question: Does a new lease or roommate reset Unit 1?
rows.answer: Not automatically. The ordinance protects specified partial occupancy changes where an original occupant remains.
rows.boundary: The reported continuing original resident and lease documents require verification.

rows.question: Is raising both units safer than one?
rows.answer: No automatic safe harbor. Examine actual reasons, consistent treatment, protected-class effects, timing, and retaliation.
rows.boundary: Owner motives, tenant activity, and protected-class facts are not established or inferred.

rows.question: Do corporate owners have a different normal percentage?
rows.answer: Ownership form can affect specific exemptions and pricing-tool duties; it does not establish a universal practice percentage.
rows.boundary: No official comparable-owner practice distribution or ownership record was verified.

rows.question: Can the increase withstand tenant-side scrutiny?
rows.answer: Only after the legal route, records, calculation, service, and nondiscrimination/retaliation checks are independently reviewed.
rows.boundary: Actual attorney review is pending; use the review packet, not an implied endorsement.

paragraphs.text: Verified rule means the cited official source supports the stated legal rule or benchmark. Reported means the user supplied the date or amount but no document was authenticated. Conditional means arithmetic or a legal consequence depends on stated assumptions. Flagged for Review means a necessary fact or independent review is missing.

Every substantive table row has an official-source link. On a private-fact row, the link identifies the rule used to review that fact; it does not certify the private fact. Blank cells are intentional, not zero values.

sections.title: Unit 1: do not assume a vacancy reset
sections.text: If Resident A was an original occupant under the owner agreement and remained in lawful possession, the reported partial occupancy change does not by itself establish a Costa-Hawkins reset. The ordinance also restricts increases imposed solely because an occupant was added. Verify the actual agreement, occupancy, and any written notices.

sections.title: Conditional arithmetic—not an authorized increase
sections.description: The Unit 1 illustration assumes the reported $3,995 is the verified base rent, the unit is covered, the effective date is in the 1.6% interval, and all timing/license/notice conditions are met. Banking, petitions, and passthroughs are excluded.

rows.reported: $3,150 at the reported Jun 1, 2019 lease start—not a current rent

paragraphs.text: A 2019 lease-start amount does not establish today's lawful rent. The missing ledger may contain lawful increases, improper charges, concessions, service changes, or other facts affecting base rent. Do not multiply the historical amount and present the result as a current recommendation.

For either unit, the complete rent history, anniversary, last increase, available banking, inventory/license status, and notice/service record must be reviewed before an amount is served or collected.

pages.title: The applicable route controls the percentage
pages.description: Local coverage is the first question. State law, federal civil-rights law, and any assistance-program terms add separate requirements; a market benchmark never overrides a rent cap.

rows.rule: 60% of published CPI, never above 7%; the published interval rate is 1.6% for Mar 1, 2026–Feb 28, 2027.
rows.application: Conditional on confirmed coverage, verified base rent, anniversary, spacing, license, and notice.

rows.rule: Unused annual percentages are additive, not compounded or rounded up; ordinary increases are limited to once in twelve months under Rule 4.12.
rows.application: No banked amount is calculated without the complete history. No cumulative cap appears in the inspected current rule/ordinance; unverified proposals are not law.

rows.rule: Covered properties: lower of 5% plus applicable CPI or 10%; published state-covered maximum is 8.8% for Aug 1, 2026–Jul 31, 2027.
rows.application: Not an elective alternative for a confirmed SF rent-controlled unit. Exemptions require document-level review.

rows.rule: Discriminatory rental terms, conditions, privileges, and related services are prohibited because of protected characteristics.
rows.application: Applies independently of the percentage. No protected characteristics are inferred.

rows.rule: FMRs are used in specified assistance programs; program terms can impose additional rent requirements.
rows.application: No general federal percentage cap was identified for the assumed private unsubsidized case, but subsidy status is blank and unresolved.

rows.rule: SF prohibits specified revenue-management devices using nonpublic competitor data; California restricts specified competitively sensitive pricing conduct.
rows.application: Owner tools and data sources are unknown. This project uses official public data and transparent arithmetic.

sections.title: Reasons that require more than an annual percentage

rows.route: O&M petition may support up to 7% additional base rent after the required comparison; debt service is excluded.
rows.evidence: Complete expense records, permitted comparison periods, allocation, filing, decision, and response to repair/hardship objections.

rows.route: Only qualifying certified work supports the ordinance's capital-improvement route.
rows.evidence: Scope, invoices, certification, allocation, applicable limits, notice, and tenant objections.

rows.route: A long tenancy below market is not itself an extraordinary circumstance; a special-circumstances petition requires more.
rows.evidence: Extraordinary circumstances unrelated to market conditions and reasonably comparable units; petition before notice.

rows.route: The ordinance generally bars an increase solely for adding an occupant, subject to its specified exceptions.
rows.evidence: Occupancy agreement, lawful possession, any authorized petition, and the actual reason for the increase.

rows.route: Banking can survive a sale; a sale does not create a new tenancy or erase rent history.
rows.evidence: Closing records, complete rent history, notices, and the legal route actually used.

rows.route: Prescribed petitions or worksheets and calculations may apply; these are distinct from ordinary base rent.
rows.evidence: Bills, utility responsibility, eligibility, prescribed forms, filing where required, and notice.

sections.title: Source discrepancies are disclosed, not hidden
sections.text: The banking summary refers to 24 full months, while Rule 4.12 uses a twelve-month frequency rule. Some agency examples also contain apparent date inconsistencies. This project follows the primary ordinance/rule and leaves banked amounts blank pending review.

pages.title: A correct percentage can still have an invalid notice
pages.description: Check the lease, anniversary, prior increase, written breakdown, service method, and lead time. A courtesy email or text is not treated as a substitute for statutory service.

rows.rule: The local anniversary and existing lease terms control when an ordinary increase can take effect; a fixed-term agreement may restrict mid-term changes.
rows.case: Anniversary and current lease form are unverified for both units.

rows.rule: Rule 4.12 permits a rent increase only once in any twelve-month period for the annual/banked route.
rows.case: Last effective increase dates are missing; do not assume eligibility from a lease date.

rows.rule: Civil Code § 827 requires at least 30 days for covered residential increases when the combined increase over the preceding 12 months does not exceed 10%.
rows.case: A standalone 1.6% ordinary increase falls on the 30-day side, but other increases and program rules must be checked.

rows.rule: The same statute requires at least 90 days when the combined increase exceeds 10%, using the statutory comparison.
rows.case: Banking and other amounts are excluded from this dashboard's calculator; do not use its 30-day result for them.

rows.rule: Personal delivery or the statute's mail service applies; incorporated mailing extensions are 5 calendar days within California, 10 elsewhere in the US, and 20 outside the US.
rows.case: No service record was supplied. Retain proof of the actual method and date.

rows.rule: SF requires the notice to identify annual/banked portions and applicable petition or passthrough components; nonconforming increases are null and void under § 37.3(b).
rows.case: No proposed notice was supplied. Rule 4.12's narrow disclosure-saving language does not excuse other ordinance defects.

rows.rule: Required reporting and a license in substantial compliance are prerequisites for annual/banked increases; suspension prevents collection during noncompliance.
For routes requiring a petition, file before serving the increase notice; prescribed worksheet routes have their own requirements.
rows.case: No petition, award, certification, or worksheet was supplied.

sections.title: Use the calculator as a planning check only

paragraphs.text: The calculator is deliberately limited to a standalone 1.6% ordinary local increase in the published interval. It does not calculate banking, petitions, passthroughs, state-cap eligibility, fixed-term lease rights, or program-specific requirements. Its date output is the latest of the supplied anniversary, twelve-month spacing date, and service lead-time date—not a legal opinion.
The overnight-delivery option uses a conservative planning buffer rather than adjudicating court days. Have the actual notice and proof of service reviewed before reliance.

pages.title: Equal percentages are not a safe harbor
pages.description: Raising one unit is not automatically discriminatory, and raising both is not automatically lawful. The actual reasons, treatment, timing, and protected-class effects matter.

sections.title: Selection scenarios a tenant-side reviewer should test

rows.assessment: Potentially lawful if supported by unit-specific verified facts; risky if timed to punish protected activity or based on a protected characteristic.
rows.records: Base-rent history, anniversary, occupancy documents, neutral policy, complaint/repair timeline, and actual reason.

rows.assessment: A longer tenancy or lower reported rent does not itself justify a market catch-up or prove discrimination.
rows.records: Current lawful rent, complete history, comparable treatment, extraordinary-circumstances evidence if asserted, and timing.

rows.assessment: Consistent percentages may support a neutral policy but do not cure an unlawful base rent, defective notice, discriminatory effect, or retaliation.
rows.records: Separate unit calculations, lawful bases, notices, policy exceptions, and protected-activity timeline.

rows.scenario: Different amounts for the two units
rows.assessment: Different dollars or percentages are not automatically unlawful when explained by lawful bases, histories, anniversaries, or approved adjustments.
rows.records: Documented unit-specific reasons and consistent application of the stated policy.

rows.scenario: Increase after a repair request or tenant organizing
rows.assessment: Retaliation scrutiny is required. The 180-day statutory provision has conditions and is not a universal safe harbor after it expires.
rows.records: Requests, complaints, inspections, organizing activity, communications, and the owner's good-faith grounds.

rows.scenario: Increase because a family member or child joined
rows.assessment: SF restricts increases solely for added occupants; familial-status discrimination and occupancy-policy issues also require review.
rows.records: Original-occupant continuity, lease terms, occupancy policy, and the actual asserted reason.

paragraphs.text: Write down the legal route and legitimate, non-retaliatory reason before selecting a unit. Use verified unit-specific facts rather than assumptions about age, family composition, disability, national origin, or any other protected characteristic. Do not infer or publish residents' protected traits.

Compare treatment across similarly situated units, explain any exception, preserve the calculation and service record, and have a tenant-side lawyer test the explanation. Consistency does not require identical dollars when the lawful bases differ.

pages.title: Ownership form changes rules—not the burden of proof
pages.description: No official comparable-owner dataset reviewed here establishes a normal corporate or individual increase percentage for Outer Sunset two-unit buildings. The project does not invent one.

rows.rule: Specified state exemptions depend on ownership form, required notices, and in some cases actual owner occupancy.
rows.limit: An individual is not automatically exempt, fair, or more likely to use a particular percentage.

rows.form: Corporation, REIT, or LLC with a corporate member
rows.rule: The specified separately alienable property exemption is unavailable to these entities under the statutory conditions.
rows.limit: Entity form alone does not establish local coverage, predatory conduct, or an algorithm violation.

rows.form: Owner occupies one of two units
rows.rule: A narrow state exemption requires principal residence at the start, continuing occupancy, and neither unit being an ADU/JADU.
rows.limit: Owner occupancy and legal unit configuration are unverified.

rows.rule: SF and California restrict specified uses of nonpublic competitor data in rent-pricing tools.
rows.limit: No tool, vendor, input data, or recommendation history was supplied for this owner.

rows.rule: DOJ's September 2026 Pinnacle announcement describes a proposed consent decree, not a final liability adjudication.
rows.limit: It is not evidence about this property and does not establish prevalence among corporate owners.

rows.rule: A legal cap and a HUD assistance benchmark are not an empirical survey of owner renewal practices.
rows.limit: No representative official corporate-versus-individual practice distribution was verified; the comparison value stays blank.

sections.title: The same tenant-side standard applies
sections.text: Ask any owner—individual or corporate—for the lawful base rent, legal route, transparent calculation, required filings, notice/service, and a legitimate non-retaliatory reason. A polished corporate policy or a small-owner explanation is not a substitute for evidence.

pages.title: A benchmark is not a rent ceiling—or an appraisal
pages.description: HUD FMRs estimate gross rents for assistance programs. Geography, year, bedroom count, and utilities must match before a meaningful comparison. Neither unit's bedroom count or utility arrangement is verified.

rows.question: Is either unit above or below market?
rows.missing: Bedroom counts, utility inclusion, condition, size, and a suitable official local comparison are unverified.

rows.question: Can HUD's value cap a private rent increase?
rows.answer: No. FMRs are assistance benchmarks, not the local lawful increase percentage.
rows.missing: Any actual subsidy or program agreement must be reviewed separately.

rows.question: Can FY 2026 ZIP values be relabeled FY 2027?
rows.answer: No. The service metadata explicitly identifies FY 2026; current-year ZIP values stay blank.
rows.missing: The FY 2027 lookup is interactive and spreadsheet retrieval failed; no extrapolation was used.

rows.question: Do these benchmarks establish normal owner behavior?
rows.answer: No. A gross-rent percentile is not a survey of corporate or individual renewal decisions.
rows.missing: No representative official practice distribution was verified for comparable properties.

paragraphs.text: FMRs generally estimate rent plus utilities, excluding telephone, at the 40th percentile of standard-quality recent-mover gross rents, subject to regulatory adjustments. That is a different measure from a sitting tenant's contract rent or a current asking-rent listing.

The FY 2027 metropolitan schedule covers three counties. It cannot be presented as an Outer Sunset or ZIP 94122 estimate. The historical ZIP series is useful context only and is not mixed with the metropolitan series to calculate a market trend.

pages.description: Fixed at the official 1.6% interval rate. This tool excludes banking, petitions, passthroughs, state-cap eligibility, and program-specific rules. It cannot determine the lawful rent.

pages.title: Make the explanation survive challenge
pages.description: This is an adverse-review checklist, not a claim of lawyer approval. No tenant lawyer, advocate, counselor, or agency has reviewed or endorsed the project. Missing facts are published as flags rather than filled with estimates.

sections.title: Questions for a critical tenant advocate or lawyer

rows.question: Is the unit covered and the base rent lawful?
rows.packet: Authoritative property record, all leases, complete ledger, notices, and any exemption/program agreement.
rows.risk: A reported age or old lease amount cannot establish today's lawful base.

rows.question: Is the timing correct?
rows.packet: Verified anniversary, last increase effective date, proposed effective date, and current lease terms.
rows.risk: The wrong anniversary, spacing, or fixed-term assumption can defeat an otherwise correct percentage.

rows.question: Is any banking traceable?
rows.packet: Year-by-year unused percentages, prior notices, license history, and an additive calculation.
rows.risk: No compounding, rounding up, or unsupported cumulative amount.

rows.question: Is the notice valid and properly served?
rows.packet: Complete proposed notice, required breakdown/forms, actual service method, date, and proof.
rows.risk: Statutory lead time and local content requirements are separate checks.

rows.question: Is the asserted reason documented?
rows.packet: The legal route, contemporaneous reason, expense/certification records if applicable, and unit-selection policy.
rows.risk: Market catch-up, a sale, or a new roommate is not a stand-alone unrestricted increase reason.

rows.question: Could the increase be retaliatory?
rows.packet: Repair requests, complaints, inspections, organizing activity, communications, and good-faith grounds.
rows.risk: The 180-day provision is conditional, not a universal safe harbor afterward.

rows.question: Is one-unit selection genuinely neutral?
rows.packet: Similarly situated unit comparisons, lawful differences, policy exceptions, and the actual decision timeline.
rows.risk: Equal treatment of both units is not a cure for discrimination or retaliation.

rows.question: Did occupancy change legally matter?
rows.packet: Original owner agreement, occupancy continuity, replacement/addition documents, and any notices.
rows.risk: A partial change with an original occupant remaining does not automatically reset rent.

rows.question: Are pricing inputs lawful?
rows.packet: Tools/vendors used, data sources, recommendations, and acceptance practices.
rows.risk: Specified nonpublic competitor-data tools are prohibited; public benchmarks are not a substitute for unit-level legal compliance.

rows.question: What can the tenant challenge independently?
rows.packet: Leases, notices, payment evidence, and the complete rent history for a Rent Board petition.
rows.risk: The Rent Board offers a tenant review route; this dashboard does not decide whether a violation occurred.
